summary: This note documents the Snowflake budget method !GET_SPENDING_HISTORY, which returns credit spending for a budget instance. It covers the syntax with optional UTC time bounds, the returned columns (MEASUREMENT_DATE, SERVICE_TYPE, CREDITS_SPENT), the privileges needed for custom and account budgets, and two example calls. The method is not available for Trial Accounts.
one_line: Reference for the Snowflake budget method !GET_SPENDING_HISTORY, which returns credit spending by date and service type.
key_facts: The method !GET_SPENDING_HISTORY is called on a budget instance as <budget_name>!GET_SPENDING_HISTORY.
This feature is currently not available for Trial Accounts.
The optional arguments are TIME_LOWER_BOUND and TIME_UPPER_BOUND, given as constant expressions in UTC timestamp format.
Both TIME_LOWER_BOUND and TIME_UPPER_BOUND must be set to limit results by a time range.
The returned column MEASUREMENT_DATE is of type DATE and gives the date when the usage occurred.
The returned column SERVICE_TYPE is of type VARCHAR and identifies the serverless feature consuming credits.
The returned column CREDITS_SPENT is of type FLOAT and gives the number of credits used.

SERVICE_TYPE values include AUTO_CLUSTERING, HYBRID_TABLE_REQUESTS, MATERIALIZED_VIEW, PIPE, QUERY_ACCELERATION, SEARCH_OPTIMIZATION, SERVERLESS_TASK, SNOWPIPE_STREAMING, WAREHOUSE_METERING, and WAREHOUSE_METERING_READER.
Viewing results for a custom budget requires a role granted the USAGE privilege on the database and schema containing the budget instance.
Viewing results for the account budget requires a specific application role, linked from the budgets documentation.
The example CALL budget_db.budget_schema.my_budget!GET_SPENDING_HISTORY() views spending for my_budget in schema budget_db.budget_schema.
The example CALL snowflake.local.account_root_budget!GET_SPENDING_HISTORY with a 7-day lower bound uses dateadd('days', -7, current_timestamp()) and an upper bound of current_timestamp().
